title: DIRECTOR OF QUALITY COMPLIANCE
text:

 **Southern Peaks, Canon City CO**
======================================================================

[Full-Time)

$75,000 To $90,000 Annually

DailyPay Available

-------------------------------------

**What You’ll Do**
==================

As a Director of Quality Compliance, you will:

Monitors compliance with applicable Colorado Department of Human Services (CDHS) Volume 7 residential licensing rules, including 12 CCR 2509-8, Section 7.714, as well as payer and Joint Commission requirements.

* Works with program leaders to draft corrective action plans for Director review and approval. Tracks deadlines, verifies completion, and escalates overdue or ineffective actions.
* Coordinates preparation for licensing inspections, payer reviews, and accreditation surveys. Organizes evidence and tracks follow-up requests.
* Tracks updates to Health First Colorado (Colorado Medicaid) and Regional Accountable Entity (RAE) requirements and works with program leaders to update procedures and audit tools.
* Conducts chart and program audits covering intake, assessments, treatment planning, service documentation, and discharge planning. Shares findings and conducts follow-up audits.
* Supervises assigned Quality and Compliance staff, coordinates audit assignments, and coaches staff on applying regulatory, payer, and accreditation standards.
* Maintains monitoring tools and trains program staff on policy changes, documentation expectations, and recurring audit findings.
* Analyzes audit results, incidents, grievances, clinical outcomes, and authorization and denial trends. Reports results to program leadership and the Director and tracks improvement actions.
* Partners with Clinical, Admissions, and Billing to monitor prior authorization, concurrent and continued-stay review, and documentation of medical necessity and level of care. Tracks denials and appeals.
* Drafts and updates procedures for Director review. Maintains current policy manuals and tracks required staff education.
* Prepares compliance reports and supporting records for leadership and board review.
* Coordinates documentation and follow-up for annual licensed independent practitioner peer review at Joint Commission accredited programs.
* Supports PREA training, audit preparation, and corrective action follow-up for assigned programs where applicable.
* Participates in quality and compliance committees and follows up on assigned actions.
* Performs other duties as assigned

**Who We’re Looking For**
=========================

You may be a great fit if you are:

✔ Compassionate

✔ Dependable

✔ Patient

✔ Team-Oriented

✔ Service-Focused

✔ Professional

✔ Positive

✔ Committed to Helping Others

**Qualifications**
==================

Required:

Bachelor's degree in social sciences, healthcare, behavioral health or related field and five years related experience OR Master’s degree and three years of experience.

* Knowledge of Colorado Volume 7 residential licensing requirements, Health First Colorado behavioral health managed care, and applicable accreditation standards is required.
* Experience with behavioral health utilization management, including authorization, medical necessity and continued-stay documentation, and payer audits. Experience in youth residential mental health or psychiatric residential treatment facilities (PRTFs) is preferred.
* Experience with Prison Rape Elimination Act (PREA) compliance, including staff training, audit preparation, and corrective action follow-up, is preferred.
* Ability to supervise and coach staff, assign work, and follow up on performance expectations.
* Ability to develop and teach methods for auditing, monitoring, and improving program operations.
* Ability to interpret and teach the application of regulations, payer requirements, accreditation standards, and contractual language.
* Knowledge of adolescent residential mental health treatment, including trauma-informed care, co-occurring conditions, and the needs of youth involved in child welfare or juvenile justice.
* Ability to develop and revise policies that meet licensing, payer, contractual, and accreditation requirements.
* Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in written form, with a diverse group of people including regulatory agency representatives, employees, clients, governing body members, and the general public.
* Must be available for periodic travel, to include overnight stays.
* Must have a valid driver’s license.
* Ability to work with computers and the necessary software typically used by the department.

**Physical Requirements (If Applicable)**
=========================================

* Ability to lift up to 25 pounds
* Ability to stand, walk, bend, and assist individuals as needed
* Ability to perform essential job functions with or without reasonable accommodation

**Apply Today**
===============

Some jobs pay the bills. Some jobs build careers. This job changes lives.

If you’re looking for meaningful work where your compassion, dedication, and hard work make a real difference every day, we encourage you to apply today.

**Join our team and become the reason someone has a better day.**
